# `silk/io/buffered_transfer`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Copy bytes from one buffered session to another, and consume only what the destination accepts.

## When to use
Use [`BufferedTransfer.transferAtMost`](#BufferedTransfer.impl.transferAtMost) or [`BufferedTransfer.transferExact`](#BufferedTransfer.impl.transferExact) inside
`silk.io.buffered_duplex.withBufferedPairCapacity` to forward a body or a stream, for example in a
proxy.

## Details
The transfer reads into the input buffer of the source and offers those bytes to the output
buffer of the destination. It consumes from the source only the bytes that the destination
accepted. If a write fails, the bytes that were not accepted stay unread in the source. No
operation allocates.

## Gotchas
The destination output buffer can still hold bytes after the transfer. Flush the destination
when the transfer is complete.

Import as `BufferedTransfer` with `import silk.io.buffered_transfer { BufferedTransfer }`.

<a id="BufferedTransfer.impl.transferAtMost"></a>

### Associated function `transferAtMost`

```silk
pub effect fn transferAtMost<'source, 'destination, SP, DP>(
  source: &mut BufferedDuplex<'source, SP>,
  destination: &mut BufferedDuplex<'destination, DP>,
  limit: usize,
  deadline: Option<Instant>,
) -> TransferOutcome
! BufferError
? &mut MonotonicClock
where &mut SP provides &ByteDuplex from &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock,
  &mut DP provides &ByteDuplex from &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Copies up to `limit` bytes from `source` to `destination`. It stops early if the source ends.

#### Details

It reads into the input buffer of `source` and offers those bytes to the output buffer of
`destination`. It consumes from `source` only the bytes that `destination` accepted. If a write
fails, the bytes that were not accepted stay unread in `source`. Nothing allocates.
`deadline` is an absolute time on the active `MonotonicClock`. `Option.none()` means no time
limit. It applies to each read and write.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure or a close made a session unusable.
- `BufferError.ReadFailed` if a read of `source` fails, or `BufferError.WriteFailed` if a write
  to `destination` fails. The failed session becomes terminal. `progress` and `accepted`
  include the bytes that this call already transferred.

#### Gotchas

The output buffer of `destination` can still hold bytes after the transfer. Flush `destination`
when the transfer is complete.

<a id="BufferedTransfer.impl.transferExact"></a>

### Associated function `transferExact`

```silk
pub effect fn transferExact<'source, 'destination, SP, DP>(
  source: &mut BufferedDuplex<'source, SP>,
  destination: &mut BufferedDuplex<'destination, DP>,
  count: usize,
  deadline: Option<Instant>,
) -> ()
! BufferError
? &mut MonotonicClock
where &mut SP provides &ByteDuplex from &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock,
  &mut DP provides &ByteDuplex from &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Copies exactly `count` bytes from `source` to `destination`.

#### Details

It consumes from `source` only the bytes that `destination` accepted. If a write fails, the
bytes that were not accepted stay unread in `source`. Nothing allocates. `deadline` is an
absolute time on the active `MonotonicClock`. `Option.none()` means no time limit. It applies to
each read and write.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.UnexpectedEnd` if the source ends first. `progress` gives the number of bytes
  that were transferred.
- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure or a close made a session unusable.
- `BufferError.ReadFailed` if a read of `source` fails, or `BufferError.WriteFailed` if a write
  to `destination` fails. The failed session becomes terminal. `progress` and `accepted`
  include the bytes that this call already transferred.

#### Gotchas

The output buffer of `destination` can still hold bytes after the transfer. Flush `destination`
when the transfer is complete.
